### Added
- **`modelManager.networkPolicy.registeredBackends`: the egress an installation allows for backends registered at runtime** (giantswarm/agent-platform#478; follows #329; bumblebee-plans#46 D3/D4/D5/D7; epic giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). model-manager starts with no backend (#329) and a backend — an in-cluster Ollama on `:11434`, an LM Studio on a node address, a Lemonade Server — is registered while it runs, as a labelled ConfigMap the chart never sees; the connectivity chart's egress policy for model-manager is rendered from the *static* backend inputs, so it did not open the registered one: under the cilium flavour `add_backend` succeeded, the backend showed on the Serving page and every model call was dropped, and the kubernetes flavour opened 443 only (`modelManager.networkPolicy.egress.cidrs` too). The new list — `{cidr, port}` and `{fqdn, port}` entries — renders one more egress rule per entry on its port in both flavours, after the static-backend rules (unchanged): `toCIDR` / `ipBlock` for a block, `toFQDNs` plus the cluster entity for a name (the cilium flavour only, exactly as the static hostname rule — so an in-cluster Service is listed by name there, Cilium's CIDR rules matching neither pods nor nodes). Empty by default, the default render is byte-identical. Guards fail the render on a `cidr` that is not an IPv4 CIDR, a missing or non-TCP `port`, an entry with both or neither destination, an `fqdn` that is not a hostname, and an `fqdn` under the kubernetes flavour with policies on, naming the cilium flavour. `make verify-managers` asserts the rule in both flavours, the untouched default and every guard; UPGRADE.md tells an operator with an enforcing policy to list a backend's destination when registering it.
